title: "Unsinkable"
subtitle: Don't ever talk about any of my plans like that again! Promise me... Promise me, my love!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Hmm ... Lights ... checked.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Width of the entrance ... checked.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Support structure for the ceiling ... checked.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Camera parrot for broadcasting the Games, hmm, very fluffy, so ... checked!
Spathodea walks slowly along the clay runway, under the wide and bright rooftop of the renovated Stadium.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Spare torch for the Uluru Flame, obstacles for Steeplechase, tenacity of the branches and temperature of the red clod ... Alright, checked! Only one more item to go before the flame lighting ceremony this midnight!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: *sobs*

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: The Uluru Flame ... Ulu? You alright?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Wh-What's with the tears?! Did I make you sad again?

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: No ... nothing. I just have sand in my eyes ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Oh, sand is common here. It gets into your eyes very easily.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Just like when my granny saw me walking for the first time.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Young lady, you should've preserved the dignity of this old flame!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Waah-ah! You burned me!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: ... Ulu, burning hot and energetic, checked.
Ticking off another check in the notebook, Spathodea looks upwards.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Safety factor of the field ... checked.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Laplace ... really did us a huge favor ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Shame I haven't had the time to talk to Ezra since we had that fight. We were both busy, and when we met, it was ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: What? You haven't talked about it? But I didn't feel anything wrong between you two ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: We did make up, that's for sure.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: But we never really talked about the fight. It's like you break your knee and just cover the wound up with trousers, as if it had never been there …

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You may feel fine when you jump and run, but it hurts whenever you sit down for a break ...
She scratches her hair and then starts to play with her fingers, a glum look on her face.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: *sighs* I wonder if Ezra and Vertin are going well with the patrol.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Relax, Flammy.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: It will be the opening ceremony tomorrow. Our checklist is even more intricately designed than a robe made with pine needles. Besides, the Bunyips haven't turned up in quite a while ...

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Everything is working like an unsinkable ship at sea. There isn't anything that may cause it to sink.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Alright ... but the last ship that claimed to be "unsinkable," um, what was it called ... um …
The stone door is opened without warning from behind the thinking girl.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Oh! I got it!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: We have an emergency!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: It's called the Titanic!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: I've bought tickets! Let me in!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: I came all the way here just for the Uluru Games, because you said that it is open to all for the first time!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Everyone, please be patient.
Holding a microphone, Makower stands on a pile of rocks, making him stand out from the group.
The whirlwind brought up by the airship only makes the travelers' steps more staggered.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: We are now standing at the entrance to the Uluru Stadium, and this is where the rumored "reincarnator" will come with flames and bring about the rain!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: The rain will comfort the thirsty travelers and soothe their dry heels!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: I guarantee you, as the ambassador of the Games, that no matter what your lineage is, you are welcome here as long as you have a ticket! All you need to do is wait patiently and with sincerity!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Sincerity? We've followed the guide and circled around the desert for a whole day!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: We need water and food! Some kids have become dehydrated!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: We need water! We need to get into the Uluru Stadium!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: That's right, yes, that's right.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Revival Squad, I'm sure you will enjoy this gift from me.

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: We need water! We need to get into the Uluru Stadium! We need water! We need to get into the Uluru Stadium!
Getting louder and louder, the rumble shakes the whole desert.
And echoes above the giant rock.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Gosh!!! It's him, that guy!!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: How shameless! We never sold a single ticket or invited so many outsiders to the Games! How can they tell such a lie?!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: He's whipping up public opinion—just his greatest strength.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I took a glance at the crowd. There are at least 3,500 of them out there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not a number Makower can incite alone. Some of them must be his accomplices. I'm sure they are good at mobilizing, swindling, blackmailing and stuff ...

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: It's the Eucalyptus Brotherhood! The leader is one of them. I know his face!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: D**n it! Seems like they're not going to make this easy for me, since I took their tickets. And there's Makower—how convenient for them!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: We can't just leave them here. Outside the Stadium, they have no food or shelter. They will suffer sunstroke in no time!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: How are you going to handle this?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Desert Flannel, do you still have those fake tickets?

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Yeah, why?

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Sell them.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Excuse me?! I thought you knew that I'm not doing this for money. I'm doing it for ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I know why you need money.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You have always wanted to buy the house where your grandmother spent her life and raised you. It's important to you, just like the Uluru Games to me and Ulu.
The young girl stands up.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Ezra, Vertin, please contact the Foundation for help. Desert Flannel, I need you to prepare to guide the crowd and maintain order!

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: Spathodea, you're not planning to ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Let's go all out, mates.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I am going.
Holding the Ulu soaked in tears in her arms, Spathodea shakes off Desert Flannel's sweaty hands.
A dry breeze follows after her, kicking up the dust and forming that shadowy gate.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Everyone, your attention, please!
The crowd's attention turns, murmurs surround the girls like a vortex.

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Ah! That is the door of the Uluru Stadium! Behind her! She is the girl in the newspaper!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: What? That girl is the "reincarnator"?

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Oh, dear, there she is! And look! That flame! Isn't that the Uluru Flame in the newspaper?

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Open the gate for us, Priestess! Show us the Uluru Stadium!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Open the gate for us! We have tickets! We have tickets!
Standing above the crowd, Makower raises his hands, showing everyone the ticket.

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Open the gate for us! We have tickets! We have tickets!
Like a summoning.
A tumultuous clamor goes up from the crowd, punctuated by Makower's questioning.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Look at those girls, my friends! That is Ms. Spathodea and Ms. Ulu!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: The newspapers have been praising them for facilitating the union of mankind and arcanists, bringing back the true spirit of sporting events, and calling them the pioneer peacemakers ...

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: In the name of the Uluru Flame, I swear it's not a lie!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Of course, of course, you are not lying. You never lie.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: No lies have been spoken. Every word was true!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: A junior student from Melbourne, an old soul, a "reincarnator." What's her attitude, and what will she do? Please find out with me!
The microphone in his hand points up at the sky, reflecting the airship's spotlight glaring down at Spathodea.
Scattering audio photos fall from the sky.

items.speaker: "Photos"
items.text: "Humans? What are they doing in the Stadium?"
People hear Spathodea's voice crystal clear.

items.speaker: "Photos"
items.text: "The world is full of sports games for humans! One after another and another!"

items.speaker: "Photos"
items.text: "Guide arcanum with science, tame the orderless power with sense" ... "And now they're even taking away the Uluru Stadium with metal bars!"

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Th-That's ...!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: How ridiculous! She said she stands for peace, yet she has never considered mankind's safety, technology, assistance, or rights!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Arcanists, arcanists ... that's all she's talking about!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: It's the voice of the Priestess? H-How could she say that ...

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: Nonsense! It is the first Uluru Games with the help of Laplace human technology. They've been talking about equality, peace and love all the time.

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: D**n you! How could you be so despicable!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: All the constructions are built by Laplace! These are all human contributions!

items.speaker: Audience
items.text: I'm out of here! It's not the Uluru Games, not the one I heard from my grandma at all!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: We should believe that she's an honest girl. She would never have lied!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Ms. Spathodea, did you really say that?
Makower passes the microphone to Spathodea, with a celebratory flair.
A Bunyip appears out of his coat. Its body starts swelling as it devours the air.
From the turmoil of lies and distrust, it gains additional power.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Flammy, confront it.

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Light it up, conquer it, and make it burn ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I will. I know what my duty is.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: You are right, Mr. Makower.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I did say that. I take responsibility for every word heard in that photo!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: But people! Listen to me!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Those words are wrong, so am I. I am a fool, an idiot, the stinkiest rotten egg in the kitchen!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I've seen countless humans on my way here, from Melbourne to Alice Springs, and then Uluru.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I've met the construction team from Laplace, the receptionist at the City Hall, the considerate doctors, and ... and my first human friend, my good friend!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: In the past, I saw humans as "the other kind." I thought they were unreasonable, cruel people who deceive others with bureaucratic jargon …

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: But now, when I think of humans, I'm reminded of …

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Of ...

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Of my friend, my gentle, brave, smart, selfless, clumsy human friend.

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Wh-What? Are you going to ...?!

items.speaker: Ulu
items.text: Confront it, light it up, conquer it, and make it burn for you.
The flame lit by Ulu burns all the way to a crawling Bunyip.
In an instant, the only thing left on the red soil is burned ashes. The Bunyip didn't even make a sound.

items.speaker: Bunyip
items.text: Ahh ... AHHH!!
The rest of the Bunyips scatter. Fleeing into the crowd and corners, causing a chorus of screams.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: And I'm willing to believe, everyone here loves sports as much as I do.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I must apologize for being an idiot with such a narrow view. I'm sorry.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Now, I hope everyone can enjoy pure sports and have fun sweating!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Those of you who have tickets, please enter the Stadium in order!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Those of you with no tickets, you can buy one from Ms. Desert Flannel for just one dollar!

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: I hereby declare the opening of the Uluru Games!
The gate is already open. Flammy puts her arms in the air as the crowd cheers.

items.speaker: Spathodea
items.text: Everyone is welcome!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: D**n it! How come ... The source has confirmed the rift between them!

items.speaker: Makower
items.text: Run, if I'm fast enough, there is still a chance.
Grabbing the camera tightly, Makower and his team hurry out of the crowd in a panic.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Or maybe, you don't deserve that chance at all.
A wall of people stand at the exit.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: We've got a helping hand.

items.speaker: Ezra
items.text: More than one hand.

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Aha ...!

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: This is what we call "the hammer of justice."

items.speaker: Desert Flannel
items.text: Take that, you s****y little long-tongue pig. I will pull your tongue out through one of your eye sockets. You should have known better than to mess with me.
